sources.entry: AgentSys by avifenesh - Workflow automation system for Claude with a group of useful plugins, agents, and skills. Automates task-to-production workflows, PR management, code cleanup, performance investigation, drift detection, and multi-agent code review. Includes agnix for linting agent configurations. Built on thousands of lines of code with thousands of tests. Uses deterministic detection (rege

summary.one_liner: agnix is a linter that validates agent configuration files (CLAUDE.md, SKILL.md, hooks, MCP configs, and similar files) across many AI coding tools before they silently break.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a Rust-based validator with 757 rules covering Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Kiro, Gemini CLI, Cline, MCP and other agent formats. It checks files such as CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, .mcp.json, settings and hook files, and reports diagnostics with file, line and rule ID. It can apply automatic fixes in safe, unsafe, or dry-run modes, and can be limited to one tool's rules with a --target flag. An explain command describes individual rules and their evidence. Output can be plain text or GitHub Actions annotations, and the project ships an npm package, pip package, Homebrew tap, Cargo crate, GitHub Action, editor extensions for VS Code, JetBrains, Neovim and Zed, and a browser playground.
use_cases: lint CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md files before committing
validate SKILL.md frontmatter so skills trigger correctly
check agent configs in CI with a GitHub Action
catch format mismatches when using several AI coding tools
notable: 757 rules across many agent tools, with rule IDs per tool family (e.g. CC-*, CDX-*, KIRO-*, MCP-*)
Auto-fix with safe, unsafe and dry-run modes that show inline diffs
Editor integrations via a language server (VS Code, JetBrains, Neovim, Zed)
agnix explain command gives the evidence behind each rule
Rust workspace split into rules, core engine, CLI, LSP, MCP server and WASM crates
caveats: Support tiers are uneven: Muse Code and Kimi Code validation is still pending, and Continue, Aider, Amazon Q, Tabnine, Codeium, Windsurf/Devin and Amp are outside active support
Roo Code support was removed in version 0.59.0
Contributor workflow requires running a preflight script with Rust, Node.js, Python and Bash
